messages:
maria: Heads-up — dashboard alerting just spiked for hosted-api latency and a bunch of 5xx from generation-service. Seeing errors post-deploy from ~2712345600. tagging oncall. 

deploy-bot: [automated deploy] canary rollout started for release v2.14.0 at 2712345595. Canary traffic 5%. 

maria: @oncall-sre paging in case this is the canary. Errors are primarily 502 / openai-compatible proxy errors and 200ms -> 2s extra P50 on embeds. 

oncall-sre: on it. grabbing logs. what's the signal on host health? 

ashley: I can see increased queue_time on the serving pool (gpu-pool-3). Memory looks steady but KV cache eviction went up. Might be flow-control issue with the new batching change. 

jordan: If this is the batching knob in the canary, we should kill the feature flag for canary quickly and scale down. Is there a kill-switch? 

maria: Yes, we have featureflag:enable_new_batching. I can flip to false if we want immediate mitigation. That would stop the new path. 

tim: Before we flip, any customers currently on dedicated? This is hosted. Customer impact report? 

maria: Quick scan: two high-revenue customers hit increased 5xx rates (acct-123 / acct-789). Support already got inbound tickets. No broad data plane outage, but SLO alerts firing. 

oncall-sre: Ok plan: 1) Pause canary by toggling flag (maria) 2) If rollback needed, prepare manual rollback to v2.13.9 (tim) 3) Drain canary nodes 4) Verify smoke tests then re-open traffic. 

maria: toggling flag now -> /ff toggle enable_new_batching false --env=canary 

maria: done. flag off returned 200. Monitoring for 60s. 

deploy-bot: [notice] Feature flag change applied to canary. 

ashley: Early telemetry — latency down slightly but not fully. 5xx rate dropped ~40%. KV evictions still high on some nodes. Might need full rollback. 

tim: Let's coordinate rollback. I'll stage manual rollback to v2.13.9 on canary pool and then pause traffic. Command I will run: 
```
infra deploy rollback --service generation-service --to v2.13.9 --scope=canary
```

jordan: Also notify PD/SM so support can hold customers. @pagerduty-bot, escalate? 

pagerduty-bot: Incident created INC-27123, paging oncall. Acknowledge to confirm receipt. 

maria: Acknowledged. Support pinged key customers with ERR code 502 and mitigation plan. 

tim: Rolling back now. Running infra deploy rollback... 

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback job 333 initiated for generation-service on canary by tim at 2712345760. Estimated 3m. 

oncall-sre: While rollback goes, begin draining canary hosts from router pool to avoid partial traffic during state transition: 
```
routerctl set-weight pool/canary 0.0
```

ashley: Drain command applied, connections are reducing. 

tim: Rollback completed on canary. Verifying versions... 

deploy-bot: [deploy] rollback job 333 finished: success. generation-service now at v2.13.9 on canary. 

maria: Reconfiguring traffic back to baseline routing: 
```
routerctl set-weight pool/canary 1.0
```

maria: Done. Observability — 5xx back to baseline, p50 returned to pre-deploy. Opening slow signal window for 10m. 

jordan: Great. Now we need smoke test checklist (post-rollback verification): 
- run healthcheck suite against canary endpoints 
- run synth load at 10rps for 5m 
- validate token accounting and embeddings consistency for sample prompts 
- ensure KV cache eviction rates are normal 

tim: Running healthcheck suite... all green. 

ashley: KV evictions dropped to baseline within 2m of rollback. Synth load looks stable. No new errors in logs. 

maria: Support update to customers sent: apology + root cause pending. Offering credit if impacted. 

oncall-sre: I'll stay on this thread for another 30m to monitor and handle any flapping. Assigning follow-up to SRE postmortem. Action items: 
- collect flame graphs and batching metrics from canary nodes 
- correlate with request size distribution 
- determine whether the batching change underestimates KV cache pressure 

jordan: Also create a rollback runbook-note: add quick kill-switch steps + who to notify for high-revenue customers. 

maria: Creating INC-27123 slack incident doc and linking to postmortem. 

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-27123 acknowledged by oncall at 2712345900. 

tim: Confirming final state: system stable, rollback successful, customers notified, follow-ups assigned. Handoff to day SRE team in 30m. 

ashley: Quick note — we should not re-rollout batching to production until we have an evaluation harness against KV cache patterns. I'll file an RFC draft. 

maria: Thanks everyone. Closing active mitigation. I'll post final incident summary in #incidents in 2 hours once we have logs. :white_check_mark: 

oncall-sre: Copy. Standing by during the watch window. 

jordan: Thanks — good quick coordination.
